reading.body:
Digital Loudoun Plaza is a three-building campus in Loudoun County, Virginia, operated by Digital Realty with a combined footprint of roughly 861,500 square feet across buildings G, H, and K, each equipped with 2N+2 cooling redundancy. The specific building represented in this record is not confirmed from available sources, so the IT load and rack count for this location cannot be stated. Digital Realty's published specifications for the campus do not include megawatt capacity, power consumption figures, or power density assumptions necessary to estimate AI training density or accelerator hosting capacity.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 have published megawatt figures in operator specifications; those 23 facilities total 1,375.4 MW of disclosed capacity. This campus does not rank among Virginia's published capacity by name, placing it outside the top 23 disclosed facilities in the state. Digital Loudoun Plaza is situated in Loudoun County, which historically concentrates Northern Virginia colocation infrastructure, but without published power figures this campus cannot be positioned relative to peers by constraint-binding metrics.

Without disclosed power consumption, this campus cannot yet be read as a factor in AI scaling. The operator's choice not to publish megawatt capacity on their spec page is itself a data point: most mapped facilities in Virginia publish nothing, and even among the largest disclosed sites, many operators do not disclose load. To assess whether Digital Loudoun Plaza matters to AI, one would need either operator disclosure of IT load, grid interconnection records, or third-party measurements not present in published sources.
